html:
In 1916, after a failed revolt against Russian rule, large numbers of Kyrgyz and Kazakhs fled over the Tian Shan mountains into Chinese Xinjiang. Kyrgyz call it Urkun, the exodus.

The revolt began in the summer of 1916, during the First World War, when the tsar ordered Central Asian men to be drafted for labour behind the front. Years of land seizures for Russian settlers under the Stolypin resettlement had already built up anger. Rebels in Semirechye, the land around Lake Issyk-Kul, attacked officials and settler villages, and many settlers were killed.

Russian troops and armed settlers struck back hard. Whole communities of Kyrgyz fled with their herds over high passes in autumn and winter. Many died of cold, hunger and attacks on the way, and many more in China. Estimates of the dead vary widely. Some survivors returned after the Russian Revolution. The revolt is a central memory in Kyrgyzstan today.
sum: In 1916, after a failed revolt against Russian rule, large numbers of Kyrgyz and Kazakhs fled over the Tian Shan mountains into Chinese Xinjiang. Kyrgyz call it Urkun, the exodus.
